clue.text: Playing option every football club would like?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: what every club would like

blocks.note: first meaning: a button on a tape or video player
second meaning, cryptic: a speedy attacking player every team wants

explanation.surface: A tactical choice that any football manager would welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: the button that winds a recording on quickly, and a quick striker any club would want to sign.
explanation.definitionFit: On a cassette or video player, the control that winds the recording on at high speed is one of the playback options.

clue.text: Your passenger is very left-wing

definitions.note: adjective phrase, while the answer is a noun for such a person

blocks.note: first meaning: someone making the same journey as you
second meaning: a sympathiser with communism who is not a party member

explanation.surface: A complaint that the person sharing your ride holds extreme socialist views.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means a companion on a journey and idiomatically a communist sympathiser outside the party.

clue.text: Distinguished gathering at the hairdresser's?

blocks.note: first meaning: a fashionable assembly of notable guests
second meaning: a hair or beauty shop

explanation.surface: A grand society meeting held, oddly, in a hair shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an elegant reception of literary or artistic figures and a business where hair is styled.

clue.text: Bellowing voice: hard to see where it is coming from?

definitions.text: hard to see where it is coming from

blocks.note: first meaning: a loud, booming way of speaking

blocks.clueFragment: hard to see where it is coming from
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: a warning horn sounded in poor visibility at sea

explanation.surface: A loud voice whose source you cannot locate.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like a puzzle about acoustics; it actually describes the weather in which the device is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a booming voice, and literally the siren sounded from ships and lighthouses when mist cuts visibility.

clue.text: But it's not the only bird that settles for the night

definitions.text: But it's not the only bird that settles for the night

blocks.clueFragment: But it's not the only bird that settles for the night
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about birds in general going to perch at dusk

blocks.clueFragment: bird that settles for the night
blocks.note: setter's reading: a male chicken, whose name sounds like 'one who perches for sleep'

explanation.surface: A naturalist conceding that many birds go to perch at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The male fowl's name looks as if it means any bird that perches overnight, which the clue concedes is not unique to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a bird, and its name is built on the verb for perching to sleep.

clue.text: A sentimental lover, name withheld, is spicy

indicators.note: something withheld is kept back, so the letter for name is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
a romantic is a soppy, sentimental lover
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An anonymous gushing lover described, oddly, as spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name withheld' reads like an anonymous admirer, but it tells you to drop the abbreviation for name from the lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Spices are valued for their strong fragrance, so a spicy dish is fragrant or pungent.

clue.text: Third cousin perhaps aloof corresponding

blocks.note: someone aloof is cool and distant
relative means in proportion or corresponding to

explanation.surface: A remote cousin described as standoffish yet keeping in touch by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding' hints at letter-writing, but here it means proportional.
explanation.definitionFit: A third cousin is an example of a family member so far removed that the kinship is remote; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Such reactionary opinions of noted oldie: why change?

definitions.note: describes such opinions; the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: a change of order is asked for, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A famous old-timer asking why anything needs to change, the creed of a reactionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the question in an old person's mouth, which happens to suit the stubborn conservatism the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from fibres dyed before spinning, means thoroughly and unchangeably committed, as entrenched reactionary views are.

clue.text: Nasty publicity to get you to have your cervix checked?

definitions.text: get you to have your cervix checked

blocks.note: first meaning: an organised effort to damage someone's reputation

blocks.clueFragment: get you to have your cervix checked
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: a health drive urging women to book a cervical test

explanation.surface: A health promotion slyly described as nasty publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a cervical screening test is commonly called a smear test, so a drive promoting it could be named this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a political drive to defame an opponent; whimsically a public-health push for screening tests.

clue.text: Seasonal cake you will make a note of, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the words before stand for a sound

blocks.note: the contraction is pronounced like the old word for Christmas
to log something is to record it

explanation.surface: Promising someone they will write down a Christmas recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate roll decorated to resemble a wooden branch is a traditional Christmas cake.

clue.text: One marsupial in love with another

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, written O
another marsupial, the Australian possum

explanation.surface: Two pouched animals falling for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' leans on the definition: it means another marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: The American opossum carries its young in a pouch, so it is one kind of pouched mammal.

clue.text: Makes inaudible doctor admit wrong to us

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of their proper order, so the next two words are reordered

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
to own up is to admit
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A doctor's quiet confession of malpractice being swamped by noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown out a sound is to cover it with louder noise so that it cannot be heard.

clue.text: In a bag, a male lizard

indicators.note: 'in' says the target sits inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of 'bag' and the next three letters

explanation.surface: A male lizard tucked into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The agama is a family of Old World lizards, often brightly coloured males.

clue.text: Upfront, never accept the offered alliance

indicators.note: what is upfront comes at the very start, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Blunt advice to refuse any proposed pact.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is a military alliance of Western nations.

clue.text: Poor at painting, I strain badly and twitch

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A struggling painter straining and twitching at the easel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking artistic skill or taste, as someone poor at painting is.

clue.text: Hurry up and squash that bug

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom urging speed, from pressing the accelerator
second meaning: literally tread on the insect

explanation.surface: Urgent instructions to be quick and kill an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a driver to press the pedal and go faster; literally it means tread on something.

clue.text: Courage to overcome shattering grief

blocks.note: to have heart is to have courage
a shattering is a break

explanation.surface: Bravery needed to get through devastating sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' places the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak is overwhelming sorrow, typically after loss or rejection in love.

clue.text: Tease lecturer about silly old soft toy

indicators.note: something silly is muddled, so the letters it governs are scrambled
moved about means shifted around, so the lecturer's letter joins the jumble

blocks.note: to rag someone is to tease them
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making fun of an academic over a daft old cuddly toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy doll made of cloth is a classic stuffed plaything for children.

clue.text: Don't know what to say? It's no way to make a sale

definitions.note: verb phrase, while the answer is an adjectival phrase meaning bewildered

definitions.text: no way to make a sale

blocks.note: first meaning: lost for words, bewildered

blocks.clueFragment: no way to make a sale
blocks.note: second meaning: selling for less than cost, which no trader wants

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's lament that selling below cost leaves them speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means baffled or lost for words, and literally describes selling for less than one paid.

clue.text: A hairstyle for each month

blocks.note: per means for each
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A monthly hair appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave is a chemically set curly style for hair.

clue.text: Cub needs aid to put on weight

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for weight
help is aid

explanation.surface: A young animal needing support to fatten up.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'put on' sets the weight letter in front of the aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog or wild animal, the same as a cub.

clue.text: A Mexico neighbour, a month back, shot at meal

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction, right to left
something shot is wrecked, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: AUG is the calendar abbreviation for August
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone from across Mexico's border was shot at dinner a month ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American country sharing Mexico's southern border.

clue.text: Girl from Morecambe area?

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Asking whether a girl comes from the seaside town of Morecambe in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the place; it is the comedian's surname, standing for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, and girl is the crossword stand-in for any woman's name.

clue.text: Men return to earth over Florida city

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
to land is to come back down to the ground
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Astronauts coming home and splashing down off Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a reversal signal, but the whole phrase means come down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a large city in central Florida, home of Walt Disney World.

clue.text: Supposing Oscar to be languishing

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
pining is wasting away from longing

explanation.surface: Imagining a man named Oscar is lovesick.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or venture an opinion, so opining is supposing or suggesting.

clue.text: Unnerves nearly defenceless slithery creature

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: to rattle someone is to unnerve them
naked can mean unprotected or defenceless

explanation.surface: A frightening, almost unprotected, slithering beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous American snake, and snakes move by slithering.
